claim: Let \(R\) be a two-loop metric rose with loop lengths \(a,b>0\). For every integer \(n\ge2\), in the connected cyclic \(n\)-cover \(\widetilde R_n\to R\) whose two loop monodromies are both \(1\in\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\), the integral cycle lattice of the connected norm kernel \(\ker(\mathrm{Nm}:J(\widetilde R_n)\to J(R))^0\) is \(A_{n-1}=\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i=0\}\), and the restriction of the ambient Jacobian quadratic form is \((a+b)\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i^2\); consequently its Gram determinant is \(n(a+b)^{n-1}\).

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: Symbolic proof supplies the all-n statement; finite script checks are supplementary only.
limits: Does not determine the separately normalized principal Prym polarization.
Does not cover arbitrary voltage assignments or general base graphs.
The proof is an explicit lattice computation; broader graph-homology theory may make this a special case.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.normalization: The form is the unscaled restriction of the ambient Jacobian quadratic form to the connected norm-kernel lattice.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.scope: Connected cyclic covers of a two-loop metric rose with both loop monodromies equal to the generator; all \(n\ge2\) and positive real loop lengths.

title: The norm-kernel lattice of cyclic covers of a two-loop tropical rose
